Use Tier 2: replace the MultVAE ensemble member with a multinomial denoising autoencoder (MultiDAE), keeping SASRec and the existing fusion procedure fixed. The latest host score is 0.5637, below the best 0.5737, with Electronics particularly weak at 0.38 HR@10. This motivates testing whether the variational bottleneck limits collaborative preference reconstruction; the aggregate results alone do not establish that diagnosis.

The primary component is model_design: retain the current encoder and decoder dimensions, replace sampled latent representations with a deterministic latent vector, and remove the log-variance head and KL penalty. Keep normalized binary training histories, input dropout, and multinomial reconstruction loss so the experiment isolates removal of variational regularization. This preserves nonlinear collaborative filtering while allowing the model to retain preference information that KL regularization may suppress.

In training_evaluation, train the replacement only on supplied training histories and select checkpoints using the same fixed validation users, candidates, and HR@10 definition. Preserve all four dataset routes, training seed 42, SASRec settings, fusion weight grid, and single-GPU execution limits. Update checkpoint metadata and the predictor writer together so validation and deployed inference reconstruct the same deterministic autoencoder and use identical fusion logic. Compare independently evaluated macro HR@10 against 0.5737, report category results, and leave held-out test prediction generation to the host.
